missionPremise: pePaywallStripe.ts's doc comment above peBillingIntervalForPriceId (verified, lines 158-166) states this repo deliberately never reads Stripe's current_period_end/plan.interval because their shape moves with the API version and nothing in this repo pins one -- confirmed by grep: zero hits for Stripe-Version/STRIPE_API_VERSION/api_version anywhere in artifacts/api-server/src, and no `stripe` npm dependency (hand-rolled fetch client only, brokerageStripe.ts stripeGet/stripePostForm). This is the exact same exclusion P-125's CP1 (_inbox/2026-09-08_p125_cp1.json, same day, same repo) named as deliberately deferred: 'renewal date (needs live Stripe current_period_end design, deliberately avoided per comment above peBillingIntervalForPriceId)'. P-129 is that deferred design, done live rather than stored.

verifiedBeforeBuild.customerResolutionSeam: readPeStripeCustomerId(userId) in pePaywallStripe.ts (lines 660-670) is the exact function createPeBillingPortalSession (A-062) already calls to resolve a PE user's Stripe customer id -- read-only, returns null for both 'no entitlement row' and 'row with null customer', NEVER creates one. Reusing it (not re-deriving) means this route and the portal route can never disagree about whose customer they are looking at.
verifiedBeforeBuild.httpClientSeam: stripeGet(path) / stripePostForm(path, params) in brokerageStripe.ts are the ONLY Stripe HTTP callers in this codebase (grep confirms). Neither sets a Stripe-Version header today. Plan: add an optional 3rd param (extraHeaders) to stripeGet only, backward compatible (its one other caller, pePaywallStripe.ts:347, passes none and is unaffected) -- this pins the version for THIS route's call only, not globally, matching the dispatch's 'for this one call' instruction.
verifiedBeforeBuild.routeNamingCollision: grep of every router.(get|post|put|delete|patch) literal path in propertyExplorer.ts: no existing /property-explorer/v1/subscription (singular). /property-explorer/v1/billing/checkout and /property-explorer/v1/billing/portal exist and are distinct. Suggested path is clear to use.
verifiedBeforeBuild.authAndErrorConventions: A-062's billing-portal route (propertyExplorer.ts ~1648-1733, tested by __tests__/pe-billing-portal.test.ts) is the direct sibling: requirePeAuthenticated middleware + a second resolvePeOwnerUserId(req) 401 check inside the handler (belt-and-suspenders, matched exactly), a discriminated-union result type (PeBillingPortalResult: portal | no-billing-account | not-configured) rather than a thrown error or fabricated field, and none of its failure arms is 500 (401/503/409/502 only). This route's result type (PeSubscriptionSnapshot: active | no-subscription | not-configured) and its route handler mirror that shape exactly.
verifiedBeforeBuild.clientWiring: hauska-map is not cloned in this worktree and is out of reach; dispatch says stop and report the contract rather than guess at client code. Will not attempt client-side wiring.
verifiedBeforeBuild.portalReplacementQuestion: Out of scope per dispatch -- building the read only (renewal date + cancellation status), reporting the portal-replacement question back rather than deciding it.

plan: 1. brokerageStripe.ts: widen stripeGet(path) to stripeGet(path, extraHeaders?: Record<string,string>), spreading extraHeaders into the fetch call's headers. No other change to the function; its one other caller (pePaywallStripe.ts) is unaffected by an optional param.

2. New file artifacts/api-server/src/lib/peSubscriptionStripe.ts: PE_SUBSCRIPTION_ROUTE constant, PeSubscriptionSnapshot discriminated union (active/no-subscription/not-configured), a pinned STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_API_VERSION constant (a real, stable Stripe API version predating the per-item billing-cycle migration that moved current_period_end off multi-price subscriptions in later API versions -- so the top-level field this route reads keeps existing), a field-by-field extractSubscriptionFacts() that returns null (never a partial object) on any missing/mistyped field, a listStripeSubscriptionsForCustomer() that calls GET /subscriptions?customer=...&status=all&limit=10 with the pinned header, filters to a locally-defined LIVE_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUSES set (active/trialing/past_due/unpaid) rather than trusting Stripe's own default list filter, and readPeSubscriptionSnapshot(userId) that composes: not-configured check -> readPeStripeCustomerId (no customer = no-subscription, never creates one) -> list+filter (zero live = no-subscription; more than one live = throw rather than guess which is 'the' subscription, since this app's checkout paths create at most one) -> extract (extraction failure = throw, never a fabricated/partial 200).

3. propertyExplorer.ts: import PE_SUBSCRIPTION_ROUTE + readPeSubscriptionSnapshot from ./lib/peSubscriptionStripe; add GET route mirroring the billing-portal route's shape -- requirePeAuthenticated + inner resolvePeOwnerUserId 401 check, not-configured -> 503 subscription_unavailable, no-subscription -> 200 { hasSubscription: false }, active -> 200 { hasSubscription: true, status, currentPeriodEnd, cancelAtPeriodEnd }, thrown error (Stripe error, ambiguity, extraction failure) -> 502 subscription_check_failed, none of these 500.

4. New test file artifacts/api-server/src/__tests__/pe-subscription.test.ts, modelled directly on pe-billing-portal.test.ts's harness (ctx.schema db mock, setupRouteTests, asUser header helper, a fetch spy with a 404-by-default arm so an unexpected Stripe path fails the test rather than passing silently). Cases: anonymous 401; free user (no stripeCustomerId) -> 200 hasSubscription:false, zero Stripe calls made; paying user with one active subscription -> 200 with the three fields, and the request URL asserted to carry the pinned Stripe-Version header (not eyeballed); a user whose subscription list returns zero live-status rows (e.g. only a canceled one) -> hasSubscription:false; two concurrent live subscriptions -> 502 (ambiguity refused, not guessed); a Stripe response missing current_period_end -> 502 (extraction fails closed, not a fabricated date); STRIPE_SECRET_KEY unset -> 503, not a simulated date; a raw Stripe error response -> 502, not 500.

completionPredicate: A live GET route exists at /property-explorer/v1/subscription, authenticated, resolving the Stripe customer the same way A-062's portal route does (no re-derivation), calling Stripe's Subscriptions API live with an explicitly pinned Stripe-Version header for that call only, returning only currentPeriodEnd/cancelAtPeriodEnd/status extracted field-by-field (never the raw Stripe object), with every failure mode (no customer, no live subscription, ambiguous subscriptions, malformed Stripe response, Stripe not configured, Stripe error) producing a declared non-2xx or explicit hasSubscription:false rather than a fabricated date or a silent null-looking 200; new tests exercise each of those states including at least one real violation per state; typecheck exits 0; a PR against main is open; the client-wiring gap and the portal-replacement decision are reported rather than built past.
scopeBasis: Dispatch scopes this lane to ONE route serving both the renewal-date read and the cancellation-flow's status read, built on the existing customer-resolution and HTTP-client seams rather than inventing new ones. Explicitly out of scope per the dispatch: touching the existing hosted-portal redirect (unless investigation showed the new route should replace it entirely -- it does not: the portal read (A-062) and this subscription read serve different purposes, portal for managing/cancelling, this route for displaying facts inline, and deciding to retire the portal redirect is a bigger call than this mission was asked to make), any client-side (hauska-map) wiring, and any Stripe secret/price-id configuration change.
